units.title: Parameters, tokens and compute as separate variables, and fixed-token versus fixed-compute contracts
outcomes: Separate parameter count, processed tokens, unique data and arithmetic compute in a run contract.
Derive fixed-token and fixed-compute comparisons with an explicit FLOP-count convention.
Budget memory and elapsed time separately from the arithmetic approximation.
units.why: Counting parameters and FLOPs supplied the arithmetic. Research comparisons now need a contract that says which resource is conserved and which effects remain entangled.

next.note: Use the contract to compare allocation methods rather than slogans.

study.title: Porian et al.: what counts as model size
study.locator: arXiv:2406.19146v1, Sections 2.1 and 2.2, Section 3.2, and Appendix B, Estimating FLOPs and accounting for attention

focus: Use \(N\) for a declared parameter count, \(D\) for processed training tokens and \(C\) for training FLOPs. Unique corpus tokens are a separate quantity when sampling repeats data.
The dense matmul estimate \(C\approx6ND\) is not an identity. Count the output projection even with tied embeddings; account separately for attention, recomputation and other omitted operations.
Fixed tokens asks about capacity at a shared exposure budget. Fixed FLOPs trades capacity against exposure. Fixed unique data permits different repetition counts. None isolates model size by itself.

Keep tokenizer, document split, context, loss denominator, architecture family and tuning budget explicit. Memory depends on microbatch and activations; elapsed time depends on the implementation, not just FLOPs.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, plan dense models with 10 million and 20 million counted parameters. At 2 million processed tokens each, \(6ND\) gives \(1.2\times10^{14}\) and \(2.4\times10^{14}\) FLOPs. At the first compute budget, the larger model instead gets 1 million tokens. Verify with integer arithmetic, then write the analogous two rows for your decoder, including output-head cost, memory state dtypes and omitted FLOPs.
traps: Tied weights reduce stored parameters but do not remove the output matrix multiplication.
Equal optimizer steps do not mean equal tokens if token batch changes. Equal nominal tokens also need the same mask and padding-count policy.
Calling equal elapsed time an IsoFLOP comparison. A kernel improvement can buy more tokens in that time without changing the statistical scaling relationship.

selfTest.q: Under \(C\approx6ND\), what happens to tokens if parameter count doubles at fixed compute?
selfTest.a: They halve. At fixed tokens, the estimated compute instead doubles; these answer different questions.

selfTest.q: Is training twice over a corpus equivalent to a corpus twice as large?
selfTest.a: No. Processed-token count can match while unique data and repetition differ. Record both and evaluate on documents excluded from training.

selfTest.q: Can equal FLOPs guarantee equal peak memory?
selfTest.a: No. State, activations, sequence length, microbatch, precision and recomputation determine peak memory. Measure feasibility separately.

units.stopWhen: Your two comparison tables conserve their declared budgets, and each row names parameter and token conventions plus the main compute and memory omissions.

fit.note: A3 supplies the comparison contract; Porian supplies parameter-count and attention-cost caveats. The mini-project applies them to the existing decoder.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: the lmlab run planner records fixed-token and fixed-compute rows, parameter-count conventions, unique and processed tokens, estimated FLOPs, measured time and peak memory.

units.title: Kaplan scaling, Chinchilla IsoFLOP profiles and why their allocations disagree
outcomes: Derive the allocation implied by a separable parameter-and-token loss model.
Distinguish sampled IsoFLOP minima, fitted valleys and the resulting frontier.
Explain the Kaplan-Chinchilla disagreement using optimization and accounting evidence, not a universal token ratio.
units.why: An allocation rule inherits the experiment that produced it. Separate the empirical frontier from a parametric fit before spending a budget on either.

next.note: Challenge the fitted loss model and its objective.

study.title: Hoffmann et al.: three allocation methods
study.locator: arXiv:2203.15556v1, Figure 1, Sections 3.2 and 3.3, and Appendix D.2, especially Equation 10

study.title: Porian et al.: diagnosing the discrepancy
Besiroglu et al.: Approach 3 replication
study.locator: arXiv:2404.10102v2, Sections 1 to 4 and Appendix A.1

focus: For \(L=E+A N^{-\alpha}+B D^{-\beta}\) with positive coefficients and exponents, substitute \(D=C/(6N)\). The stationary condition is \(\alpha A N^{-\alpha}=\beta B D^{-\beta}\), not equality of the two reducible-loss terms unless the exponents match.
This yields \(N_*=(\alpha A/(\beta B))^{1/(\alpha+\beta)}(C/6)^{\beta/(\alpha+\beta)}\). Equal growth follows only when \(\alpha=\beta\). Twenty tokens per parameter is not a universal constant.
Porian isolates output-head FLOPs, excessive warmup and scale-dependent optimizer tuning. Matching decay changes loss but does not by itself explain the allocation gap in that study.
Besiroglu challenges Approach 3 rounding, optimizer termination and intervals using reconstructed data. That does not invalidate the separate IsoFLOP evidence or establish a law for your decoder.
units.reproduce: Derive the stationary condition without notes. As an arithmetic audit, use the rounded Equation 10 constants \(E=1.69\), \(A=406.4\), \(B=410.7\), \(\alpha=0.34\), \(\beta=0.28\) and \(C=5.88\times10^{23}\) FLOPs. Obtain approximately 32.491 billion parameters and 3.01622 trillion tokens; compare with a one-dimensional numerical minimization and require relative allocation error below \(10^{-5}\). This is the rounded published fit, not a recommendation or a reproduction of Chinchilla. Explain the mismatch using Besiroglu.
traps: Fitting a valley when every sampled point is still descending. An optimum outside the sampled range is not identified.
Treating the historical allocation exponents as percentages of actual dollars or wall-clock time.
Repeating the introductory IsoFLOP fixture from Counting parameters and FLOPs and calling it a new measured result.

selfTest.q: Why does the additive floor not change the fixed-compute optimum in this model?
selfTest.a: It is constant in \(N\) and \(D\), so its derivative vanishes. Estimating it can still change the other fitted parameters and hence the estimated optimum.

selfTest.q: What allocation exponents follow from \(\alpha=0.34\) and \(\beta=0.28\)?
selfTest.a: Approximately 0.451613 for parameters and 0.548387 for tokens. They sum to one under \(C=6ND\), but are not both 0.5.

selfTest.q: Does Porian show that decay never matters?
selfTest.a: No. It can improve loss substantially. The claim concerns its limited role in explaining the allocation discrepancy in their tested setups.

practice.name: TensorTonic: Recover an IsoFLOP Compute-Optimal Frontier
practice.locator: Fit a quadratic in \(\log N\) at each compute budget, then a log-space frontier across the recovered minima.
practice.note: Free. The public cases supply square-root and four-tenths-power frontiers with guaranteed interior positive-curvature minima. Add your own boundary-minimum rejection test. These are supplied-data drills, not measured scaling evidence.

units.stopWhen: Your analytic and numerical allocations agree, your frontier code rejects an unsupported valley, and you can explain both the Porian and Besiroglu caveats.

fit.note: The allocation papers, their two critiques and the named free frontier drill cover derivation and preparation without repeating the earlier A3 fixture exercise.
